correctness.rationale: For n≥8 the full four-subset kernel has the Newton expansion of s↦q^((4−s)²) at s=0 into the PSD matrices M_j M_jᵀ, with the degree-four term F(q)I. The first four coefficients are positive for 0<q≤1/3; F changes sign between 1/4 and 1/3 and is decreasing up through 13/25 by the displayed derivative bound. At the root, the lower incidence column spaces nest in that of M₃, so rank reduces to rank M₃. The column-independence induction works because the exchange of x,y passes from (t,k,n) to (t−1,k−1,n−2) within t≤k≤n−t, forcing adjacent t-set coefficients equal and hence zero. On eight points the degree-four and degree-three pair differences are eigenvectors by flips and unpaired-coordinate symmetry. Counting flips gives F and G=1−2q+2q⁹−q¹⁶, respectively; G=(1−q)(1−q⁸)(1−sum_{i=1}^7 q^i), which is negative on [13/25,1) by even the first four terms of the sum. Thus between the first root and 13/25 the degree-four form is negative, and beyond it up to 1 the degree-three form is negative. The eight-point matrices are principal submatrices at every n≥8, and unit diagonal ensures a positive direction. The all-ones endpoint is separate. At 19/20 a bounded numerical check gives F≈0.00616653 and G≈−0.07962785, consistent with the rational signs; for general n the degree-three eigenvalue counts one choice preserving the unpaired point and n−7 choices adding one unit to the distance, hence equals F+(n−6)γ₃ and is negative there as well. value.rationale: A radial kernel usable on every ground-set size has an explicit, size-independent admissible set and an exact rank at loss of strict positivity. The same finite obstruction excludes every high-q interval; the top harmonic's sign reversal shows why recording only the first transition is insufficient in this natural distance family. This is a full classification rather than a numerical bandwidth or one small matrix computation.
